criterion_scores.reasoning: I checked the three changed code paths plus the numbered YED-227 decisions. The overall mechanism is in the right place, but the runtime-ledger classifier is too coarse and can excuse a missing reference based on text co-occurrence rather than a real append-only writer, which violates Decision 1.

The artifact covers the required pieces: check-refs skip logic, shared helper, build_graph mirror, and selftests. The gap is that the build_graph integration test can be skipped entirely when no missing runtime ledger exists on disk, so the new behavior is not always exercised.

Placement and naming look correct for this repo: the shared helper lives under .claude/hooks/, build_graph imports it from the hooks path, and no house naming or MCP/subagent convention is violated in this diff. I did not find a convention breach beyond a minor inline assumption in comments.

The change factors the rule into one helper instead of duplicating logic, avoids placeholders, and does not introduce unnecessary ceremony. The main risk is the heuristic text-scan approximation, but that is already captured as a correctness issue rather than an anti-pattern problem.

There are useful selftests and failure messages, and the comments explain the intended rule. However, the docstring also asserts an unverified repo-wide claim as if it were established fact, which weakens the honesty/traceability of the diagnostic framing.

defects.description: The runtime-ledger heuristic can promote a ledger to the skip set by co-occurrence rather than actual append-only writing. Because the code later treats any name found by this heuristic as exempt, a read-only or typo'd .claude/artifacts/*.jsonl reference can be skipped when it should still flag. That contradicts the spec's 'only when some tracked script writes that ledger only in append mode' rule.

defects.description: The new YED-227 integration selftest is conditional on a currently missing runtime ledger existing on disk. If the repo state changes and no such ledger is absent, the test returns True and the new check-refs/runtime-ledger path is not exercised at all, leaving the change under-tested in that state.

defects.description: The helper states a repo-wide scope assumption as fact without any citation or mechanical proof. That is an unverified confidence claim about repository state, and it matters because the skip logic depends on it.
